==English== [[File:Hans Rottenhammer - Allegory of the Arts - WGA20147.jpg|thumb|A [[painting]] showing many kinds of art, including [[literature]], [[music]], and painting itself.]] ===Etymology 1=== {{wikidata lexeme|L1348}} {{etymon|en|:inh|enm:art|tree=1}} {{root|en|ine-pro|*h₂er-}} From {{inh|en|enm|art}}, from {{der|en|fro|art}}, from {{der|en|la|artem}}, accusative of {{m|la|ars||art}}. Partly displaced native {{noncog|ang|cræft}}, whence {{w|Modern English}} {{m|en|craft}}. See also archaic {{noncog|en|list|t=art, craft, cunning, skill}}. ====Pronunciation==== * {{IPA|en|/ɑːt/|a=RP}} ** {{audio|en|En-uk-art.ogg|a=UK}} * {{IPA|en|/ɑɹt/|a=GA}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-art.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɑː(ɹ)t|s=1}} * {{hyphenation|en|art}} {{col-top|2|Other accents and pronunciations}} * {{IPA|en|[ɑːʔ]|a=Estuary English}} * {{IPA|en|[äˑɹt]|[-ɻ-]|[ɑˑɻt]|a3=Ulster|a=Ireland}} * {{IPA|en|[aːt]|[äːt]|[ɒːt]|a3=Geordie|a=Northern England,Wales}} * {{IPA|en|[ɒət]|[ɒɹt]|a2=rhotic|a=NYC}} * {{IPA|en|[ɑ̈ɹt]|[ɐɹt]|a2=Atlantic Canada|a=CA}} * {{IPA|en|/ɐːt/|[äːt]|a=AU,NZ}} * {{IPA|en|/ɑːt/|[ɑːtʰ]|[-tsʰ]|a=South Africa}} {{col-bottom}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[conscious]] [[production]] or [[arrangement]] of [[sound]]s, [[colour]]s, [[form]]s, [[movement]]s, or other [[element]]s in a manner that affects the senses and emotions, usually specifically the [[production]] of the [[beautiful]] in a [[graphic]] or [[plastic]] [[medium]]. #: {{ux|en|There is a debate as to whether graffiti is '''art''' or vandalism.}} #* {{quote-book|en|date=May 3 1992|chapter=[[w:List of Jeeves and Wooster episodes|Comrade Bingo]]|title=w:Jeeves and Wooster|section=Series 3, Episode 6 |passage=''[[w:Bertie Wooster|B.W. Wooster]]:'' If you ask me, '''art''' is responsible for most of the trouble in the world.
''[[w:Jeeves|R. Jeeves]]:'' An interesting theory, sir. Would you care to [[expatiate]] upon it?
''[[w:Bertie Wooster|B.W. Wooster]]:'' As a matter of fact, no, Jeeves. The thought just occurred to me, as thoughts do.
''[[w:Jeeves|R. Jeeves]]:'' Very good, sir.}} #* {{quote-journal|en|year=2005|month=July|author=Lynn Freed|journal=Harper's |passage="I tell her what Donald Hall says: that the problem with workshops is that they trivialize '''art''' by minimizing the terror."}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2009|author=Alexander Brouwer |passage=Visual [[art]] is a subjective understanding or [[perception]] of the viewer as well as a deliberate/[[conscious]] arrangement or creation of elements like [[colour]]s, [[form]]s, [[movement]]s, [[sound]]s, [[object]]s or other [[element]]s that produce a [[graphic]] or plastic whole that expresses thoughts, ideas or visions of the artist.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The creative and emotional expression of [[mental imagery]], such as visual, auditory, social, etc. # {{lb|en|countable}} Skillful [[creative]] activity, usually with an [[aesthetic]] focus. #: {{ux|en|She's mastered the '''art''' of programming.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} The [[study]] and the [[product]] of these processes. #: {{ux|en|He's at university to study '''art'''.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[aesthetic|Aesthetic]] [[value]]. #: {{ux|en|Her photographs are nice, but there's no '''art''' in them.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[artwork|Artwork]]. #: {{ux|en|Sotheby's regularly auctions '''art''' for millions.}} #: {{co|en|'''art''' collection}} # {{lb|en|countable}} A [[field]] or [[category]] of art, such as [[painting]], [[sculpture]], [[music]], [[ballet]], or [[literature]]. #: {{ux|en|I'm a great supporter of the '''arts'''.}} # {{lb|en|countable}} {{lb|en|often in dichotomy with {{m|en|science}}}} A subject understood best through [[intuition]] rather than [[methodology]]. #* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-03|volume=408|issue=8847 |title=[http://www.economist.com/news/finance-and-economics/21582498-america-has-changed-way-it-measures-gdp-boundary-problems Boundary problems] |passage=Economics is a messy discipline: too fluid to be a science, too rigorous to be an '''art'''. Perhaps it is fitting that economists’ most-used metric, gross domestic product (GDP), is a tangle too. GDP measures the total value of output in an economic territory. Its apparent simplicity explains why it is scrutinised down to tenths of a percentage point every month.}} # {{senseid|en|studied skill}}{{lb|en|countable}} [[skill|Skill]] that is attained by [[study]], [[practice]], or [[observation]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1796|author={{w|Matthew Lewis (writer)|Matthew Lewis}}|title=w:The Monk|page=217|publisher=Folio Society|year_published=1985 |passage=A physician was immediately sent for; but on the first moment of beholding the corpse, he declared that Elvira's recovery was beyond the power of '''art'''.}} #* '''1855''', {{w|Harriet Martineau}}'s translation, ''The Positive Philosophy of Auguste Comte'' Vol. 1, Introduction, Ch. 2, [https://archive.org/details/positivephilosop01comt/page/n68/mode/1up?view=theater page 21,] from {{w|Auguste Comte}}, ''Cours de philosophie positive'' (1830–1842) #* {{RQ:Churchill Celebrity|chapter=IV|page=58|passage=The Celebrity, by '''arts''' unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no hand in the furnishing of that atrocious house.}} # {{lb|en|uncountable|dated}} [[contrivance|Contrivance]], scheming, manipulation. #* {{RQ:Shelley Poetical Works|I|The Revolt of Islam|222|it was not '''art''',
Of wisdom and of justice when he spoke—
When ’mid soft looks of pity, there would dart
A glance as keen as is the lightning’s stroke
When it doth rive the knots of some ancestral oak.}} #* {{RQ:Emily Bronte Wuthering Heights|volume=I|chapter=VI|page=112|passage=[...] and Mrs. Earnshaw undertook to keep her sister-in-law in due restraint, when she returned home employing '''art''', not force—with force she would have found it impossible.}} =====Synonyms===== * {{sense|Human effort}} {{l|en|craft}} =====Antonyms===== *
